title: CordataProvenanceRunFacet
description: What was declared, and what authorised it. Emitted as `cordata_provenance` on every run event, terminal or not. The point of the whole block is that an auditor can get from a published number back to the reviewed commit without asking anybody.

descriptor_path.description: Path of the descriptor this run executed, relative to the repository root.

descriptor_sha256.description: Hash of the descriptor bytes as they were when the run started — not as the file looks today.

source_table.description: Fully qualified name of the source the run read.

source_schema_version.description: The catalog version the descriptor pinned, and therefore the shape the input actually had.

descriptor_git_commit.description: The commit that last touched the descriptor. Null outside a repository — absence of provenance is not the same as bad provenance, and a consumer reading null knows to ask.

descriptor_git_commit_signed.description: Whether that commit's signature verified against a trusted key (git's `%G?` returning G). A run whose provenance points at an unsigned commit is itself a finding.

executor_version.description: Name and version of the executor that ran this.

step_params.description: Parameter values substituted into the declared steps, keyed by step id. Where a model version lives, which is usually the most audit-relevant fact about a scoring run.
